messages:
mira: Quick RFC follow-up: IPv6-only customers + NAT64. We need to decide whether to preserve customer source IP across peered control plane vs relay fallback, or accept SNAT and document caveats.

ben: Preserve-src keeps customer ACLs and CDN rate-limits stable but introduces ENI/IP management and attach latencies.

tess: Product sees two cohorts: ACL-sensitive and best-effort. An opt-in flag makes sense.

liam: Ops constraints: relays are ephemeral and don't have per-tenant ENIs by default. ENI attach ~15-25s on peak; quotas vary by instance type.

mira: Options: A) Default SNAT on failover (simple). B) Opt-in reserved IP lease (control-plane issues IP lease; relay attaches ENI on failover). C) Stateful L4 proxy to preserve 5-tuple across path changes (complex).

ben: B is pragmatic: pre-warm ENIs for high-need tenants or attach on-demand with documented fallback to SNAT. C is fragile because NAT64/conntrack replication is tricky.

tess: Recommend default=A, API opt-in=B, C=experimental for top-tier only. Include billing note for reserved IPs and SLA caveats.

infra-bot: NOTE: implementer checklist: ENI quota template, automation for pre-warm, monitoring for attach latency/failures, runbook for fallback to SNAT.

liam: Action items: ben -> API + pricing text; tess -> customer doc + test matrix (DNS64, NAT64, TCP/QUIC); mira -> architecture doc with lease lifecycle; infra-bot -> quota template + metrics.

mira: I'll record decision: default SNAT; opt-in preserve_src via reserved IP lease; stateful proxy as limited beta.

all: no objections.

infra-bot: REMINDER: Any ENI churn feature requires oncall escalation updates.
